what_its_for: Etonogestrel is a hormone used to prevent pregnancy. It is a small, thin, flexible rod (about the size of a matchstick) that is placed under the skin of your upper arm by a healthcare provider. It releases a low, steady dose of the hormone progestin to stop you from getting pregnant for up to 3 years.
how_to_take: You do NOT take this medication by mouth. A specially trained doctor or nurse will numb your upper arm and insert the small rod just under the skin. The procedure takes only a few minutes. You should be able to feel the rod under your skin but should not see it. After insertion, keep the bandage on for 24 hours and the small pressure bandage on for 3 to 5 days. Check regularly that you can still feel the rod. If you cannot feel it, contact your healthcare provider and use a backup birth control method such as condoms until the rod is confirmed to be in place.
dosing: There is only one rod inserted at a time. It releases a continuous low dose of etonogestrel (about 60–70 micrograms per day when first inserted, gradually decreasing over time). It provides pregnancy protection for up to 3 years. After 3 years, the rod must be removed and, if desired, a new rod can be inserted at the same time.
missed_dose: Because the implant works automatically once inserted, there are no doses to miss. However, if the implant has been in place for more than 3 years, it may no longer be effective. Contact your healthcare provider to have it replaced on time. If you think the implant may have moved or you cannot feel it, use backup birth control (like condoms) right away and call your provider.
storage: The implant is stored and handled by your healthcare provider before insertion. Once inserted in your arm, no special storage is needed. The insertion kit (before use) should be stored at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C) and kept away from direct sunlight and moisture.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking certain medications that can make the implant less effective at preventing pregnancy, including some seizure medications (like phenytoin, carbamazepine), rifampin (an antibiotic), HIV medications, and St. John's Wort (an herbal supplement). Always tell ALL of your doctors and pharmacists that you have the implant. Avoid smoking, especially if you have other health risks, as it can increase certain health risks with hormonal birth control. Do not try to remove or adjust the implant yourself.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you: cannot feel the implant in your arm; have severe abdominal or stomach pain (could signal a problem with pregnancy or a cyst); notice the implant seems to have moved or is sticking out of the skin; have signs of a blood clot such as sudden chest pain, shortness of breath, severe headache, vision changes, or leg pain and swelling; have heavy or unusual vaginal bleeding; develop yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice); think you might be pregnant; have signs of infection at the insertion site such as redness, swelling, warmth, or pus; or experience depression or major mood changes.
when_it_works: If the implant is inserted within the first 5 days of your menstrual period, it works to prevent pregnancy right away. If it is inserted at any other time during your cycle, use a backup birth control method such as condoms for 7 days. Most people experience changes in their period — some may have lighter or no periods, while others may have irregular or more frequent spotting. This is normal and not a sign that the implant is not working.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do not use if you are pregnant or think you may be pregnant. The implant must be removed if pregnancy is confirmed. Breastfeeding: Etonogestrel passes into breast milk in very small amounts. It is generally considered safe to use while breastfeeding, typically inserted 4 weeks after delivery, but discuss with your doctor. Teens: The implant can be used in adolescents after their first menstrual period. Older adults: The implant is not typically used after menopause. Liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have liver disease, as this medication may not be right for you. Obesity: The implant is generally effective regardless of body weight, but discuss any concerns with your provider.
